hits.tldr: Tailwind CSS scans source as plain text, so you must use complete class names and map dynamic values to predefined class lists.
Tailwind CSS scans project files for class names and generates only the CSS styles actually used.
Tailwind scans source files as plain text for tokens matching expected class name characters, then generates CSS only for recognized utilities.
Use `--value([{type}])` syntax to declare which data types arbitrary utility values support.
Use inline styles in Tailwind for dynamic values from APIs/databases and complex arbitrary values.

structuredContent.query: arbitrary value bg-[url()] not detected dynamic class name JIT

content.text:
Your fix is correct and expected behavior. Per `src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx` ("Dynamic class names" section): Tailwind scans source files as plain text, so it can't understand Laravel's `{{ Vite::image(...) }}` interpolation — the class string `bg-[url('...')]` never exists as a complete, literal token at build time, so no CSS is generated for it.

Since the URL comes from a dynamic source (Vite's asset helper), the docs recommend inline styles for exactly this case (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "When to use inline styles"): use `style="background-image: url('...')"` — which is what you did.
